issues.title: Certified neutral overwrites the raw response intensity with 0.0
issues.defect: `_response_intensity()` returns 0.0 whenever certified response direction is neutral, instead of preserving the source-scale coordinate or absence.
issues.evidence: Accepted v5 and runtime both contain this at lines ~284–290.
issues.consequence: Raw source measurement is corrupted; midpoint 0.5 and absent values collapse into the canonical signed zero.
issues.required: Preserve raw `response_intensity` exactly. Only `v551_signed_intensity` is zero for certified neutral.
tests: Neutral raw missing stays missing; signed 0.0.

issues.title: `response_intensity_status` can contradict the persisted intensity
issues.defect: Status is computed from the original row while `_response_intensity()` can coerce neutral to 0.0. This permits an atom with `response_intensity=0.0` and `response_intensity_status=MISSING`.
issues.evidence: Accepted/runtime lines ~284–323; validator has a missing-intensity-coerced-to-zero protection path.
issues.consequence: The same field carries mutually inconsistent value/status semantics.
issues.required: Compute value and status from the same preserved raw coordinate. Neutral signed zero belongs only in signed projection fields.
tests: Neutral missing yields response_intensity null + status MISSING.

issues.title: Intensity-only response-family logic can certify direction without direction authority
issues.defect: If all direction fields are blank, an approved response family plus numeric intensity is treated as a certified directional response (`CERTIFIED_INTENSITY_ONLY`).
issues.consequence: Direction is inferred from response-family/intensity presence even though accepted scale-v5 authority forbids runtime inference where direction/geometry are unresolved.
issues.required: Remove intensity-only certification. Missing certified direction is a nonpromotable repair reason, never a certified atom basis.
tests: Numeric intensity + no certified direction → repair candidate, no atom.

issues.title: Directionality stamp audit wrongly requires raw intensity for certified neutral
issues.defect: The stamp audit marks every expected row missing/incomplete whenever `response_intensity` is absent, with no neutral exception.
issues.evidence: Runtime helper lines in `build_v551_directionality_stamp_audit`: `if intensity is None: failures.append("missing_response_intensity")`.
issues.consequence: Lawful neutral rows with explicit direction but absent raw coordinate are falsely counted as missing stamps and can block readiness.
issues.required: Make intensity required only when the governing scale/projection semantics require a coordinate/magnitude. Certified neutral may be complete with raw intensity absent.
tests: Neutral + map matched + certified direction + raw missing → STAMPED.

issues.title: The directionality expectation helper trusts a contaminated applicability field
issues.defect: The helper is conceptually designed as an applicability denominator, but it uses `current_directional_atom_eligible`, which is already contaminated by full V551 eligibility gates.
issues.evidence: Helper docstring explicitly calls field canonical applicability denominator; V550-001 shows field semantics are not pure.
issues.consequence: Coverage still excludes some failed rows and therefore understates missing stamps/repair debt.
issues.required: Switch helper to the new immutable directional-applicability contract introduced under V550-001.
tests: Rows failing response map/structure still appear in expected denominator when authority says directional.

issues.title: Certification candidate bridge is already promotability-filtered
issues.defect: Candidate construction requires `v551_relation_evidence_eligible`, matched response map, joined QUC/source structure, certified semantic/directionality authority, complete mapping, usable-for-evidence, and support conditions before a row even becomes a candidate.
issues.consequence: Rows that should be visible as nonpromotable repair debt are removed before adjudication; distribution completeness cannot account for them.
issues.required: Build the candidate universe from directional applicability + direct substantive response identity. Move row-level success/failure conditions into per-candidate adjudication outcomes.
tests: Bad candidate appears in adjudication/repair surface while clean sibling still promotes.

issues.title: Known-bad candidates are emitted as atoms and only rejected later by strict validation
issues.defect: Paths such as intensity-only direction can pass early eligibility, fail signed projection, still produce an atom row, then the strict validator marks `unresolved_signed_projection` and fails the run.
issues.evidence: Accepted validator flags unresolved signed side/intensity; current builder can generate `BLOCKED_REGISTRY_PROJECTION_REQUIRED`/unresolved projection.
issues.consequence: Candidate-level defects become whole-run failures and contaminate the clean atom pack.
issues.required: Adjudicate before atom emission: only PROMOTABLE candidates may enter `relation_evidence_atoms`; all known nonpromotable candidates go to repair output. Keep atom validator strict.
tests: One bad row does not suppress clean sibling atoms.
All emitted atoms pass strict contract validation.

issues.title: V551 run integrity is conflated with evidence sufficiency and candidate defects
issues.defect: Readiness booleans and final status gate on atom count, missing stamp rows, missing eligible-bridge atoms, unresolved projection rows, and pressure-eligible rows. A valid compiler run with zero promotable atoms is treated as not ready/failure.
issues.evidence: Runtime compiler lines ~417–427 include `len(atoms) > 0` and pressure row requirements in readiness.
issues.consequence: The pipeline cannot represent valid no-evidence or all-repair outcomes; row defects masquerade as compiler corruption.
issues.required: Separate `run_integrity_status`, evidence/adjudication status, and downstream-operation sufficiency. Hard-fail only unsafe compiler/authority/schema invariants.
tests: Zero promotable + valid adjudication → integrity PASS with typed evidence state.
